_README: TRANCHE 11 - PATCH. The last three raw-blank surfaces, all inside choose_one option values.
Nothing here touches body_text - only option values.
1. initial_cotenancy_optional_2
was: 'and/or __________________ [IDENTIFY KEY TENANT(S)'
now: 'and/or {{param:initial_cotenancy_key_tenants}}'
Two defects in one value: an 18-underscore raw blank, and an UNBALANCED instruction
bracket. Your note field shows the source as '[OPTIONAL:  and/or __________________
[IDENTIFY KEY TENANT(S)]' - the closing bracket belongs to the inner instruction and was
lost when the outer [OPTIONAL: ...] gate was stripped at extraction. The instruction is
stripped entirely (it is guidance, never emitted) and the blank is keyed.
Kept as `fill`: key tenants are identified by the dealmaker, not the landlord.
2. utilities_optional_1
was: 'in excess of an aggregate of $____________'
now: 'in excess of an aggregate of ${{param:utilities_fee_cap}}'
The '$' stays outside the token - it is fixed text, and a value carrying its own currency
symbol would drift. 'an aggregate' needs no article param: the following word is fixed.
`fill` - this is a negotiated cap on extraordinary fees, wizard-answered.
3. eu_remedy - AND THIS IS NOT THE audit_blank_1 PATTERN. You and I both guessed it was.
was: '...percentage rent of ___ percent (__%) of Tenant's gross sales...'
now: '...percentage rent of {{param:eu_remedy_pct_word}} percent
({{param:eu_remedy_pct_num}}%) of Tenant's gross sales...'
audit_blank_1 is ONE STRING appearing twice - 'seven percent (7%)' both times, byte
identical. Here the two blanks take DIFFERENT RENDERINGS of one number: 'five percent
(5%)'. Word form before 'percent', numeral inside the parentheses. One param cannot serve
both without emitting 'five percent (five%)' or 'five' where '5' belongs.
So: two params, both DERIVED BY OVIS from a single negotiated rate - the same arrangement
as audit_article, where OVIS derives a dependent form rather than anyone entering it twice.
The assembler does no computation, so the derivation has to happen upstream. Nothing in
the payload asserts the two agree; if you want that guarded, it belongs in OVIS at
resolution time, not in the assembler.
FOUR THINGS FOR YOU, none of which I have keyed a decision into:
A. SINGLE-OPTION CHOOSE_ONES. All three of these are choose_one with exactly one option,
which violates the standing per-tranche rule 'no single-option choose_ones'. I have NOT
changed that, because I think the rule now has a legitimate exception and that is your
call, not mine. All three are [OPTIONAL: ...] constructs in the template - include this
text or omit it. Since contract A made `omit` a first-class param kind, the two states are
'this option' and {"kind": "omit"}, and the option set genuinely has one member. The rule
predates the omit sentinel. Either amend it to exempt optional constructs, or these three
get re-keyed to something else - tell me which.
B. eu_remedy sits at sort_order 1 with no option 0, which you flagged. That is consistent
with A: option 0 is the not-used branch and was never materialised because nothing
represented it until `omit` existed. Worth checking whether the other two are also
sort_order 1, and whether anything downstream assumes sort_order starts at 0.
C. THE TWO PYLON BLANKS SHOULD BE landlord_fill, NOT fill - confirmed against Powder Springs,
which carries Mike's own margin comments on exactly those blanks: 'LL please insert
dimensions' on the dimensions blank and 'LL please enter location of monument' on the
location blank. Same evidence class as the CAM/pro-rata landlord_fill re-key.
sign_pe_blank_4 / sign_pn_blank_5 -> landlord_fill, render '__________'         (10)
sign_pe_blank_3 / sign_pn_blank_4 -> landlord_fill, render '__________________' (18)
I have NOT included that change here because it is a param-kind change across two bodies I
just superseded in tranche 10, and stacking a second supersession on the same bodies in
consecutive tranches is how a body ends up orphaned. Say the word and it is tranche 12.
D. sign_pn_choose_2 UNRESOLVED IN THE FIXTURE - Mike's call, not mine and not yours.
Powder Springs emitted 'on both sides of the monument or pylon sign(s)' - neither option,
the CHOOSE carried through unresolved. Two readings and they lead opposite ways:
(i) an oversight in the send. Then the acceptance test records it as a KNOWN FIXTURE
DEFECT with an expected diff, exactly like SALE OF PROPERTY stripping, and the
library stays as it is.
(ii) deliberate - for a to-be-constructed sign it may genuinely not be settled which
structure gets built, and 'monument or pylon' is the honest term. Then it is a third
legal option and the library is missing it.
Do NOT add the third option on my guess. Asking Mike.
